sentence: This project uses whole-brain imaging of single cells to find out how brain networks change during alcohol abstinence and how treatments reduce addiction-like behaviors.
This project studies how a small RNA in liver immune cells stops liver cancer in mice by restoring the immune response against tumors.
This project studies how natural bypass arteries form and tries to find ways to make them grow after heart injury.
This project builds ways to study repeat elements in the genome and uses them to screen for ovarian cancer without invasive tests.
This project provides genomic research services and equipment that help investigators find genes linked to disease and to normal tissue function.
This project tries to find out how membrane vesicles from harmless mouth bacteria work and whether they could help prevent gum disease.
This project builds noninvasive imaging tools that show metabolism in the body, to help study diseases such as cancer, stroke and heart disease.
This project tests whether a program that supports long-term yoga practice keeps helping veterans with chronic low back pain.
This project builds fast methods to change the genes of the nematode C. elegans so that gene function and gene failure can be tested.
This project provides training in biomedical informatics and data science that supports precision medicine.
This project studies how autophagy can be boosted without starvation to protect cells from damage in the eye of Drosophila.
This project tries to find out how a protein called TTYH1 controls fat storage and fat release in support cells of the brain.
This project tests and improves a way to sequence fetal DNA from maternal plasma, so pregnant women can avoid invasive procedures.
This project studies how two gene changes affect lung cancer growth and tests whether blocking an enzyme that handles fats helps treatments work.
This project uses 3D bioprinting to build a working artery platform that shows how hypertension changes the vessel matrix and vascular reactivity.
This project studies how kidney disease raises the level of certain fat molecules and whether a medication can lower them.
This project brings together research on muscular dystrophy, including gene therapy tools and blood markers, and provides shared resources for other researchers.
This project tries to find out how heme, which is made inside mitochondria, is moved to the proteins that use it in the cell.
This project studies how dopamine changes the activity of receptors that respond to glutamate in the nucleus accumbens.
This project studies how a protein shapes the development and function of helper T cells during long-lasting infection.
